issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is dead code.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag the `break` immediately after `raise` as unreachable. It signals the author was undecided between fail-fast and aggregate-all-misalignments semantics. Pick one policy, document it, and remove the dead statement.

issues.description: Raising a class named `PerformanceWarning` as a fatal exception is a category error.
issues.detail: `PerformanceWarning` is by name and convention advisory — used with `warnings.warn`. Raising it as a hard exception (and asserting it with `pytest.raises`) conflates notification with abort and locks in the wrong shape. Either rename to a proper `Error` subclass and raise, or call `warnings.warn` and proceed.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` computation is incoherent and exposes a leaky internal value to users.
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` uses a meaningless `max(1, itemsize)` guard (itemsize is always >=1) and presents the result to users as the value to set `array.chunk-size` to, though the relation isn't linear. State the precondition you want the user to satisfy instead of inventing a number.

issues.description: Only `dw[0]` is inspected; the verdict is rendered for the entire axis.
issues.detail: `normalize_chunks` can produce uneven tail chunks, but the check only examines the first chunk per axis. Either verify every chunk on each axis is divisible by the shard size, or state and document why first-chunk inspection is sufficient.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` relies on operator precedence — write `!= 0`.
issues.detail: Python's precedence makes this work by accident. A reader must simulate the parser to verify correctness. Replace with `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` for clarity and to remove a needless trap for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Misalignment policy belongs at a different module boundary, not embedded in `to_zarr`.
issues.detail: Deciding what to do when `array.chunk-size` config conflicts with shard shape is a policy/config-resolution concern; embedding it inline in `to_zarr` strengthens its precondition based on global config and leaks config semantics into the write mechanism. Extract a `_resolve_write_chunks(z, config)` helper with a stated contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously refuses the patch as not ready. Three structural defects dominate: dead code (unreachable `break` after `raise`), a category error (raising a class named `PerformanceWarning` as a fatal exception, cemented by `pytest.raises` in the test), and an incoherent `safe_chunk_size` calculation surfaced to users as actionable config advice. Secondary issues include inspecting only the first chunk per axis, relying on operator precedence in the divisibility predicate, and embedding global-config policy inside `to_zarr`. The underlying idea — use shard shape as `previous_chunks` for alignment — is sound; the implementation must decide warn-vs-raise, drop the dead break, fix the size math, and verify all chunks before resubmission.
